title: Reference Source: 80,188 checkable reference facts with per-record source provenance
description:
80,188 facts across 214 reference datasets. Every record carries the URL of the page it was taken from and the verbatim sentence on that page which states it.

Most reference data on the web asks to be trusted, and a plausible number becomes indistinguishable from a checked one once it has been copied twice. Every record in this deposit therefore carries, beyond the value itself: source (the page it came from), source_quote (the exact line on that page stating it), verified_fields (those mechanically confirmed to appear inside that quote) and derived_fields (those that are the compiler's classification rather than the page's words). Any record can be checked against its source without reference to the compiler. Where a source does not state something the row is omitted rather than estimated, so gaps are deliberate.

What verification means here: the value was mechanically confirmed to appear inside the quoted line, and the quote confirmed to appear on the cited page. It does not mean a human has adjudicated the underlying question, and it is not a claim that the source is correct.

Coverage is uneven by design. Datasets are extended until their sources are exhausted, across multiple passes; a dataset covering part of its territory is not claiming completeness. Where a jurisdiction is absent it is usually because its source could not be retrieved from an official host, and the dataset's source list generally records what was omitted and why.

Scope. Chiefly US and EU regulatory, standards, technical-compatibility and jurisdictional reference data: exposure limits, statutory thresholds and deadlines, standards crosswalks, software version compatibility, shipping and hazard classifications, licensing and eligibility rules.

Currency. Reference data decays and the re-checking is the substantive work. Each dataset carries last_verified and stale_after. This deposit is a dated snapshot; the continuously re-verified version is at referencesource.org.

Rights. The facts and this compilation are offered under CC BY 4.0. Individual facts are not copyrightable (Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service, 499 U.S. 340 (1991)); the selection, verification and arrangement are the compiler's. The source_quote fields are short verbatim excerpts from the publishers named in source, reproduced so a reader may check the value; no rights are claimed over them and each is attributed and linked. Where a source's own terms govern reuse, those terms govern, and several datasets record that position explicitly.
